consensus_summary: No settled consensus. Frequent associations are the setting sun (endings/decline/death/darkness), the east-west merism for totality or infinite distance (esp. Ps 103:12 sin removal), Hebrew yam as sea/seaward (Mediterranean), and westward approach to God's presence (Holy of Holies at the west end of the tabernacle/temple).
book_summary: The sea at the back: Hebrew for west is “sea” (yam); Israel faces east, so west is “the hinder sea,” what lies behind; and as far as the east is from the west, so far are the transgressions removed.
consensus_core_identification: Unsettled multi-valent: sea/seaward (yam), sunset/endings/death, merism for distance/totality, or approach to divine presence.
book_core_identification: The hinder sea (yam), what lies behind; and the east-west distance of sin removal.
boundary_disagreement: Book centers only the linguistic-geographic hinder-sea/behind sense plus the Ps 103 merism, omitting the sunset/death/darkness and tabernacle-presence associations that are primary or common across the consensus responses.
rationale: All consensus responses mark the absence of a single settled meaning and list the yam/sea association together with the Ps 103:12 distance merism as common alternatives. The book selects precisely those elements, specifying them as “the sea at the back / hinder sea / what lies behind,” which preserves the consensus category while narrowing its extension and precision; the result is refinement, not equivalence to a unified core, contradiction, or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus responses frequently elevate or equally weight the sunset/death and tabernacle-orientation meanings that the book entry does not address, so the entry may appear selectively incomplete.
